wiki-iran.standing: The Wikipedia article on Iran, and how many people open it each day. Attention to a country page rises and falls with the events that put it in front of people, so the curve is a rough record of when the world was looking at Tehran.
wiki-iran.recent: Readership has fallen by about a third across the month, from the 19 July peak down to the 8 August low, as the Strait of Hormuz shifted from war to negotiation: Trump halted attacks on Iran's infrastructure, and talks with Oman on reopening the strait made progress. It has not gone quiet — US missiles crippled a cargo ship in the Gulf of Oman on 11 August.

brent.standing: The price of a barrel of North Sea crude, and the benchmark most of the world's oil is sold against. It moves on supply — a strike, a sanction, a strait — and fuel, freight and fertiliser move after it.
brent.recent: The premium built through the Strait of Hormuz standoff has drained as Trump halted attacks on Iran and talks with Oman moved toward reopening the lanes, though transit is still conditional and only 8 to 15 ships cross daily. Drone strikes on Russian refining at Novorossiysk and Nizhnekamsk, and a third fire at Libya's Zawiya refinery, have not put it back.

wti.standing: The price of a barrel of US light sweet crude, the benchmark American oil is sold against and the reference for US fuel prices. It moves on supply and policy, and diesel, freight and airfares move after it.
wti.recent: Crude has fallen roughly a fifth over the window despite strikes on Libya's Zawiya refinery and two Russian refineries, and a drone attack on Nizhnekamsk that killed 13. Futures eased on Trump's 'good talks' comment on Iran and on Hormuz reopening hopes, though US diesel still costs $5.36 a gallon.

natgas-hh.standing: The US benchmark price for natural gas, set at a Louisiana pipeline hub and the reference for American gas contracts. It tracks weather-driven heating and cooling demand, storage levels and export capacity, and electricity bills follow it.
natgas-hh.recent: US gas prices drifted to a 60-day low of $2.56 on Aug 7, down from $3.34 on May 29, with no domestic supply shock in the window. The demand story is elsewhere: SpaceX is building its own natural gas power plants for a Texas chip factory rather than waiting on the grid, and Amazon is funding a Fort Stockton plant whose 35 turbines could emit 33 million tons yearly.

wheat.standing: The world price of milling wheat, the grain that feeds more people than any other. It sets the cost of bread and flour across importing countries, and governments that subsidise loaves carry the difference on their budgets.
wheat.recent: Wheat has climbed 13.75% over the series to $199.6/mt, well above the September 2025 low of $155.1 and off the May 2026 peak of $220.9. The FAO's food price index hit 131.1, and the cost is landing on importers: a 20kg flour bag in Karachi now costs Rs3,000, and Punjab farmers are marching over it.

rice.standing: The world price of a tonne of milled rice, the staple grain for roughly half the planet. It is set by a thin export market — a handful of countries sell most of it — so an export ban or a bad monsoon in one of them lands on import bills everywhere.
rice.recent: Rice has moved the other way from the rest of the food basket: the series is down 29% to $400 a tonne, well below its Aug 2024 high of $563.8 and near the Oct 2025 low of $330.6. That falls against the Food and Agriculture Organization's index hitting 131.1, a three-year high driven by heatwaves and wars pushing up crop costs.

copper.standing: The world price of refined copper, the metal that carries electricity in every wire, motor and transformer. Because nothing is built or electrified without it, its price is read as a gauge of construction, grid work and industrial demand.
copper.recent: The series has climbed roughly half again over the window, to $13,550 a metric ton in June 2026 against a low of $8,910 in December 2024, and the input does not explain the move.

us-10y.standing: The interest rate the US government pays to borrow for ten years, and the rate against which mortgages, corporate debt and much of the world's borrowing is priced. It falls when money seeks safety and rises when it seeks yield.
us-10y.recent: The peak came on Jul 31, when the BOJ held rates at 1% and warned underlying inflation was exceeding its 2% target; the yield hit 4.75%, up from 4.38% on Jun 26. It has held near 4.7% since, with the dollar at its weakest since May and a Fed split leaving a rate hike in doubt.

sp500.standing: The main US stock index, tracking the 500 largest listed American companies, and the benchmark most equity portfolios and pension funds are measured against. It is the reference price for global risk appetite.
sp500.recent: The index reached 7758 on Aug 7 after a run from its Jun 10 low of 7267. The coverage does not explain the move: it concerns the plumbing around equities rather than their prices — Crypto.com launching derivatives tracking 1,500 US stocks, and $1.32 trillion in stock perpetuals on CoinGecko data.

nasdaq100.standing: A market-cap-weighted index of the 100 largest non-financial companies on the Nasdaq exchange, heavily concentrated in chipmakers, software and platform firms. It is the closest thing markets have to a single price on the technology trade.
nasdaq100.recent: The index sits near the top of its range after recovering from a Jul 29 low of 27190, with the capital story running through AI buildout: Nvidia arranged $500 billion of financing through six lenders for customers buying its chips, Amazon is funding a 35-turbine gas plant in Fort Stockton to power a datacentre, and DRAM jumped from $39 to $145.

us-gas-retail.standing: The average price American drivers pay at the pump, surveyed weekly across the country. It follows crude oil with a lag of a week or two, and it is the single price most visible to US households, which makes it a political number as much as an economic one.
us-gas-retail.recent: Refineries have been the target rather than the wells: Ukrainian drones hit two Russian refineries on 6 August and reached Nizhnekamsk, 1,600 km from the border, on 10 August, killing 13, while a third drone strike burned Libya's Zawiya refinery on 11 August. A fire at Saudi Aramco's Jizan facility was extinguished on 9 August.

natgas-ttf.standing: The European benchmark price for natural gas, set at a Dutch virtual trading hub and quoted per million British thermal units. It sets what the continent pays to heat homes, run power stations and make fertiliser and steel.
natgas-ttf.recent: Prices are up roughly a quarter over the window, well off the December 2025 low of 9.46 and below the March 2026 peak of 17.67. The input does not explain the move.

vix.standing: A measure of how much movement traders are paying to protect against in the US stock market over the coming month, derived from S&P 500 option prices. It rises when investors buy insurance and falls when they stop bothering.
vix.recent: The index has drifted down through the summer to 15.28, near its 63-day low of 14.9 on Aug 7, well below the 22.22 peak on Jun 10. The same calm shows up in crypto: bitcoin volatility nearly vanished as ETFs took in $754 million, and traders read the sell-off from $65,000 as thin volume rather than panic selling.

fx-pkr.standing: The rupee's price against the dollar. Pakistan imports most of its fuel, edible oil and machinery, so the rate sets domestic prices, and it is the number the central bank spends reserves to hold steady.
fx-pkr.recent: The rupee has barely moved in a month, trading in a narrow band between 276.5 and 278.2 while the pressures on it built underneath. The finance ministry has forecast inflation of 9-10% on the war shock, diesel prices now change daily, truckers are still striking and Jamaat-e-Islami counted 510 protests in a day over the petroleum levy.

fx-ngn.standing: The exchange rate between Nigeria's naira and the US dollar. Nigeria earns most of its foreign currency from crude oil exports, so the rate tracks oil receipts and central-bank reserves, and it sets the cost of nearly everything the country imports.
fx-ngn.recent: The naira held in a narrow band, easing about 1.2% over the month from its Jul 22 high of 1381 to 1363. Abuja approved deep offshore tax incentives pitched at unlocking $50 billion in oil investment, and the Senate opened audit hearings that Seplat Energy skipped — but neither moved the rate far, and the input does not explain the drift.

fx-egp.standing: Egypt's currency against the dollar. The pound sets the price of everything Egypt imports — wheat, fuel, medicine — and its level is the single most consequential number for household costs in a country of over a hundred million.
fx-egp.recent: The pound has drifted stronger over the month, from 51.37 on Jul 25 to a low of 49.56 on Aug 8, now 50.22. Nothing in the coverage explains the move, though it runs alongside a drug pricing freeze that turned a devaluation into empty pharmacy shelves in Cairo, and a drone strike on the Damietta gas hub days after Europe staked its gas supply on that port.

fx-try.standing: The exchange rate of Turkey's currency against the dollar. A managed float with heavy central-bank involvement, it is the price at which Turkish households, importers and the state's large foreign-currency debts are settled, and its slide has been chronic rather than episodic.
fx-try.recent: The lira drifted to a fresh 30-day low against the dollar as Turkey pushed on two fronts: a defence pact signed in Mecca with Saudi Arabia and Pakistan on 7 August, and a law passed on 10 August to disarm Kurdish separatists. Neither event produced a break in the currency's steady one-way decline.

fx-bdt.standing: The Bangladeshi taka against the US dollar. Bangladesh imports its fuel, wheat and industrial inputs in dollars and earns them back through garment exports and remittances, so the rate sets the cost of living and the margin of the country's largest industry.
fx-bdt.recent: The taka held a narrow band, easing from 124 on Aug 7 to 123.2 with a low of 122.7 on Jul 16 — a range too tight to attribute to any single event. The month's Bangladesh news ran to politics rather than trade: India's denial of involvement in Hasina's planned virtual address, and the unsigned Teesta water treaty with Delhi.

fx-idr.standing: The Indonesian rupiah against the US dollar. Southeast Asia's largest economy runs on imported fuel and dollar-denominated debt, so the rate sets the cost of both — and Bank Indonesia's policy is judged against it.
fx-idr.recent: The rupiah's firmest stretch of the month followed Prabowo's nomination of a Bank Indonesia deputy as the central bank's new governor, on which the currency rose slightly; it reached 17,800 on Aug 8 and trades near 17,870, down about 1.1% from the Jul 28 high of 18,110.

fx-lbp.standing: The Lebanese pound's exchange rate against the US dollar. Long fixed by the central bank, it collapsed during Lebanon's banking crisis and now trades at a rate that sets the price of nearly everything in a country that imports most of what it consumes.
fx-lbp.recent: The pound has barely moved, holding near the top of its 30-day range after peaking on Aug 7. The pressure on Lebanon is physical rather than monetary: Israeli strikes and demolitions across the south, a seventh round of direct talks in Rome, and 4,333 killed in the south since March by the Lebanese count.

fx-cny.standing: China's currency against the dollar, managed within a daily band set by the People's Bank of China rather than floated freely. Its level sets the price of the world's largest manufacturing base, so it moves export margins, commodity demand and trade politics.
fx-cny.recent: The yuan drifted to a 30-day high against the dollar, reaching 6.744 on Aug 13 from 6.775 on Jul 18 — a move of well under half a percent. Factory and services activity shrank in July on extreme weather and weak demand, and Beijing tightened drone exports as another trade clash with Washington built. Neither produced a decisive move in the currency.

fx-inr.standing: The exchange rate between India's rupee and the US dollar, and the price at which the world's most populous country buys its oil, chips and dollar debt. A weaker rupee raises the cost of every import and every dollar repayment.
fx-inr.recent: The rupee firmed to 95.35 from a 96.65 high on Jul 18, with a 30-day low of 95.05 on Aug 5. India's July retail inflation rose to 4.45% from 4.38% in June, a food-price story — onion prices rose 22.54% — while the Federal Reserve remains split on rates, setting the dollar side of the pair.

fx-brl.standing: The exchange rate of Brazil's currency against the US dollar, and the price at which the country's soy, iron ore and coffee earnings convert home. It moves on domestic politics and on US rates, and Brazilian import prices and dollar debt costs move with it.
fx-brl.recent: The real weakened through a month of friction with Washington: the US revoked the visa of Brazil's ambassador on 4 August, tying its restoration to Brasília accepting its own envoy pick, and the Workers' Party nominated Lula for a fourth term on 2 August, opening a presidential race with no successor named. The currency sits at its weakest of the window.

fx-mxn.standing: The exchange rate between the Mexican peso and the US dollar, one of the most heavily traded emerging-market currencies. Mexico sends most of its exports to the United States, so the rate tracks the health of that trade relationship.
fx-mxn.recent: The peso strengthened to 17.06 per dollar, its firmest of the past month and down from 17.54 on Jul 19. Nothing in the month's Mexico coverage — the $25 million US bounty on a CJNG leader, the Sinaloa Cartel's split, the screwworm outbreak past 500 cases — accounts for the move.

fx-eur.standing: The exchange rate between the euro and the US dollar, quoted here as euros per dollar. It is the world's most heavily traded currency pair, and the rate sets the import price of energy and commodities — sold in dollars — for the whole euro area.

fx-jpy.standing: Japan's currency, priced against the dollar, and the funding leg of the world's largest carry trade. A weak yen flatters Japanese exporters' earnings and raises the cost of everything the country imports, starting with energy and food.
fx-jpy.recent: The yen strengthened to a one-month high on 3 August after Japan and the US made a joint intervention, pushing the dollar down; Tokyo had already sold dollars for yen hours before the Bank of Japan held rates at 1% on 31 July, and declined to confirm that earlier move. The cheap yen it followed nearly doubled Toyota's quarterly profit to $9.4 billion.

fx-rub.standing: The exchange rate of Russia's currency against the dollar. It is the clearest daily price on how much oil and gas revenue is reaching Moscow and how much sanctions, war risk and capital controls are squeezing it.
fx-rub.recent: The ruble weakened through early August as Ukrainian drones reached targets deep inside Russia — a strike on Nizhnekamsk, 1,600 km from the border, killed 13, and Novorossiysk's port and naval base were hit on 12 August. Moscow's rejection of a Ukraine freeze on 9 August and Putin's threat to seize Western cargo ships closed off any near-term easing.

fx-zar.standing: The exchange rate of South Africa's currency against the dollar, and the most heavily traded currency in Africa. It carries the country's commodity exports and its borrowing costs, and swings on capital flows more than most emerging-market peers.
fx-zar.recent: The rand firmed through the window, reaching 16.15 against the dollar on Aug 8 from a high of 16.83 on Jul 25 — a move of about 1.2%. The coverage does not name a driver for it.

btc.standing: The largest cryptocurrency by market value, traded around the clock and secured by miners who compete to add blocks. It is the asset most crypto prices track, and the collateral behind exchanges, ETFs and corporate treasuries.
btc.recent: A run of custody failures set the tone: attackers drained Foundation's and Citadel21's Lightning nodes, and a Coldcard hack took $120 million, with the attacker's own transactions congesting the network. Bitcoin fell 4% against every other market signal and sits 49% below its record, even as ETFs took in $754 million.

eth.standing: The second-largest cryptocurrency by market value and the settlement layer for most stablecoins, tokenized assets and decentralised exchanges. Its price moves with speculative flows, and the applications built on it move after.
eth.recent: The month has been flat within a narrow band, with the high on Jul 27 and the low on Jul 18 barely 6% apart. Nothing in crypto's news flow has moved price: over 100 crypto projects folded in 2026, Crypto.com launched tokenized derivatives tracking 1,500 US stocks that carry no share and no vote, Treasury sanctioned Iranian dollar-token exchanges, and Brazil imposed a 24-hour delay on transfers above $10,000.

paxg.standing: A dollar price for one troy ounce of gold, the metal held as a reserve asset by central banks and as household savings across much of Asia. It pays no coupon, so it competes with interest-bearing assets and rises as real yields fall.
paxg.recent: Spot gold reached $4,392 an ounce on Wednesday, a ten-week high, as markets positioned ahead of the July US CPI print — the release that sets expectations for Federal Reserve cuts and, through them, the dollar and real yields. In Pakistan, where gold is priced per tola and functions as the household savings system, the rupee's own depreciation stacks on top of the dollar move.

wiki-artificial-intelligence.standing: A count of how many people open Wikipedia's article on artificial intelligence each day. It is a rough gauge of public curiosity about the technology rather than of the technology itself, rising when AI reaches people who do not follow it professionally.
wiki-artificial-intelligence.recent: Readership climbed through a week in which a model designed 16 working virus genomes, Nvidia arranged $500 billion in lending to finance chip purchases, and Meta released its Glimmer weights to run on a single consumer GPU. The 11 August peak followed Zuckerberg's 6,500-word manifesto on superintelligence.

wiki-russia.standing: The Wikipedia article on Russia, and the number of people who open it each day. Reading it is a rough gauge of how many people are trying to orient themselves on the country — its geography, government and history — rather than follow a single story.
wiki-russia.recent: Attention tracked the war reaching Russia's interior: the peak on Aug 8 sat between a drone strike on Nizhnekamsk, 1,600 km from the Ukrainian border, that killed 13, and Moscow's rejection of a Ukraine freeze, with Galuzin ruling out anything short of the root causes. Ukraine then struck the naval base at Novorossiysk.

wiki-pakistan.standing: A daily count of how many people open the English Wikipedia article on Pakistan — a rough gauge of when the country enters the world's attention, and of which events pull outsiders toward the basics rather than the headline.
wiki-pakistan.recent: Attention peaked on 29 Jul and has drifted lower since. The 7 August signing in Mecca of a joint defence pact between Saudi Arabia, Turkey and Pakistan drew the widest coverage in the window, alongside a suicide attack on a peace rally in Swat district on 2 August that killed 14.

wiki-china.standing: Wikipedia's article on China, one of the most-read country pages on the site. Daily readership of a country's page is a rough gauge of how many people worldwide are looking that country up, and it rises when something there breaks into the news.
wiki-china.recent: The peak on 10 Aug came as China evacuated over a million people ahead of Typhoon Dolphin's landfall at Yuhuan, having closed major ports a full day early. Readership stayed elevated into 12 August with the death of former premier Zhu Rongji at 97, whose restructuring of state firms and WTO accession cost tens of millions of jobs.

wiki-strait-of-hormuz.standing: The sea lane between Iran and Oman that carries the exports of the Gulf's oil and gas producers. There is no route around it, so what happens in a channel a few miles wide sets prices for crude and LNG worldwide.
wiki-strait-of-hormuz.recent: Readership has fallen by roughly two-thirds from its 14 July peak as the closure settled into a stalemate. Iran keeps the strait shut behind six conditions and a reparations demand, with 8 to 15 ships crossing daily; Trump says the US owns it, and Tehran says there is no progress on reopening.

wiki-bitcoin.standing: The number of people reading Wikipedia's Bitcoin article each day — a rough gauge of how far the subject has spread beyond people who already hold it, and one that rises with newcomers and shocks rather than with price alone.
wiki-bitcoin.recent: The window was dominated by custody failures rather than price: a Coldcard hack drained $120 million and congested the mempool with the attacker's own transactions, a firmware bug let thieves take $88 million from a hardware wallet maker, and attackers drained Foundation's and Citadel21's Lightning nodes. Bitcoin sits 49% below its record.

wiki-saudi-arabia.standing: A daily count of how many people open the English Wikipedia article on Saudi Arabia — a rough gauge of when the kingdom, the largest Gulf oil producer and the custodian of Islam's two holiest sites, pushes into global attention.
wiki-saudi-arabia.recent: The peak on 23 July preceded the diplomacy that followed: Erdogan sat down with Riyadh and Pakistan's army chief, and on 7 August Saudi Arabia, Turkey and Pakistan signed a joint defence pact in Mecca that names no obligations and never states whose nuclear deterrent applies. Houthi missiles hit Marib and wounded 11 in Najran the same week.

wiki-donald-trump.standing: The Wikipedia article on the sitting US president, and one of the most-read biographies on the site. Its daily readership rises and falls with what the White House does, making it a rough gauge of how much of the world's attention American politics is holding.
wiki-donald-trump.recent: Readership peaked in mid-July and has drifted down since. The August news ran through Washington rather than around it: Trump halted attacks on Iran's infrastructure and claimed the US fully controls the Strait of Hormuz, denied a munitions shortage while Hegseth requested $67 billion, and 25 states sued over tariffs on 60 economies.

wiki-india.standing: The Wikipedia article on India, the world's most populous country and a nuclear-armed democracy of more than a billion people. Its daily readership is a rough gauge of how much global attention the country is holding.
wiki-india.recent: Views drifted down through the window, from 32,800 on 14 July to 27,230. The month's news was domestic and dispersed rather than singular: Modi inaugurated the Param Pragya AI supercomputer at Sonipat, Parliament enabled fees on the free Unified Payments Interface, and officials geoblocked Bitchat's GitHub code.

wiki-israel.standing: Daily readership of the English Wikipedia article on Israel — a rough gauge of how many people are looking up the country's basics rather than following a specific story, and one that rises whenever it dominates the news elsewhere.
wiki-israel.recent: The peak on Aug 11 came as Venezuela restored ties with Israel after 17 years and as more than 500 attacks hit the West Bank in a week. Netanyahu rejected the Gaza withdrawal plan on an election calendar set for October 27, while strikes and demolitions continued in south Lebanon.

wiki-ukraine.standing: Daily count of how many people open the English Wikipedia article on Ukraine — a rough gauge of how much of the world is paying attention to the country at any given moment, and one that falls between shocks even when the war does not.
wiki-ukraine.recent: Readership has drifted down through a month of strikes that no longer break new ground: Russian missiles hit a children's hospital in Kyiv and war-risk premiums closed Odessa's ports to shipping, while Ukraine struck refineries at Yaroslavl and Nizhnekamsk, 1,600 km from the border, killing 13. Moscow ruled out a freeze on 9 August.

wiki-nigeria.standing: The Wikipedia page for Nigeria, and the daily count of people reading it. Africa's most populous country and its largest oil producer, so attention to it tends to rise with elections, security incidents and shifts in the crude market.
wiki-nigeria.recent: Readership fell back from its 27 July peak as Nigeria's news moved from politics to industry. The August stories were sectoral: aviation unions struck at Lagos airports, barricades sealed Air Peace terminals, and Tinubu approved deep offshore tax incentives pitched at $50 billion while July crude output fell 4% month-on-month.

cp:hormuz.standing: One-fifth of global seaborne oil passes through this 21-mile strait between Iran and Oman.
cp:hormuz.recent: Iran keeps the strait closed, setting six conditions and adding a reparations clause as the deal window narrows to a week; 8 to 15 ships now cross daily against a 44-vessel peak on Jun 24. US missiles crippled a civilian cargo ship in the Gulf of Oman on Aug 11, and Trump said of the strait, "We own it.

cp:bab-el-mandeb.standing: Between Yemen and Djibouti — the Red Sea’s southern gate. Houthi attacks since 2023 have pushed container shipping to reroute around Africa.
cp:bab-el-mandeb.recent: Traffic has thinned as Houthi attacks moved from threat to sinking: a projectile sank the Indian-flagged MSV Faize Noore Oliya on 4 August, and a strike on a cargo ship killed six sailors. Crossings fell to 18 on 3 August from 28 two days earlier and bottomed at 14 on 5 August, with escort requests up 39% since February.

cp:suez.standing: Egypt’s 120-mile artery carries roughly 12% of global trade. The 2021 closure disrupted supply chains for weeks; Red Sea instability keeps it volatile.
cp:suez.recent: The southern approach remains the constraint: a Houthi strike in Bab al-Mandeb killed six sailors, and a projectile sank an Indian-flagged vessel in the Red Sea. Transits have settled near 48 a day since the 16 June trough of 21, with the past week level against the 90-day baseline.

cp:malacca.standing: Between Malaysia and Sumatra — the fastest route between the Indian and Pacific Oceans. Over 80,000 ships a year, including most of China’s oil imports.
cp:malacca.recent: Traffic sits near its 90-day baseline, down 1.8 percent over the last week. The one visible dislocation is upstream: Hormuz vessel transits have fallen to a fraction of normal and Gulf crude arriving in Malaysia has dropped, which changes what tankers carry east rather than how many pass. Nothing in the strait itself explains the move.

cp:taiwan.standing: Between mainland China and Taiwan — roughly 40% of the world’s container traffic passes through, and the flashpoint of any US–China confrontation.
cp:taiwan.recent: Traffic ran about a fifth below its own baseline after Typhoon Dolphin: China shut major ports a full day before landfall on 8 August and evacuated over a million people, and the 10 July trough of 28 vessels bracketed a similar disruption. Chinese coast guard ships also drifted off Orchid Island, east of Taiwan, on 31 July.

cp:panama.standing: 50-mile shortcut between the Atlantic and Pacific. Drought in 2023–24 cut daily transits by half — a live example of climate binding to trade.
cp:panama.recent: Transits have slid to 29 a day, down about 15% across the window and 4.8% below the 90-day baseline, with a peak of 83 on Jul 13 and a trough of 22 on Jul 22. The input does not name a cause for the decline.

cp:bosporus.standing: Istanbul’s 20-mile waterway links the Black Sea to the Mediterranean — the only route for Russian naval access and Ukrainian grain exports.
cp:bosporus.recent: Traffic fell as the war moved onto the water: drones sank a Rosatom freighter near Novorossiysk on 1 August, struck the Turkish-operated Nadezhda on 4 August, and hit the Novorossiysk naval base again on 12 August. Turkey has since turned back some vessels bound for Novorossiysk, rationing passage.

cp:gibraltar.standing: 8 miles between Morocco and Spain — the only Atlantic–Mediterranean link. A surveillance chokepoint for Russian submarines and sanctioned oil.
cp:gibraltar.recent: Traffic has held flat. The strait is running at 112 vessels a day, level with its own 90-day baseline over the past week, and the whole 87-day window spans only 111 on Jun 3 to 163 on Jun 13. There is no move here to explain.

cp:dover.standing: The busiest shipping lane on Earth — 400+ ships a day squeeze through the English Channel’s 21-mile narrows.
cp:dover.recent: Traffic sat near the bottom of its 87-day range in early August, with the low of 126 on Aug 3 falling in the same window as the Channel small-boat crossings — a dinghy carrying about 160 people caught fire off Boulogne-sur-Mer on 4 August, and a record 230 people reached the UK on a single boat. The input does not otherwise explain the decline.

cp:cape-of-good-hope.standing: The 3,000-mile detour around southern Africa — the alternative when the Red Sea is closed. The new default for tankers since Houthi attacks began.
cp:cape-of-good-hope.recent: Traffic has halved across the window, from 161 vessels a day on 15 May to 83, with the low of 68 on 4 July. Rough weather and waves up to 3.8m mark the latest readings. The coverage does not explain the decline.

cp:kerch.standing: Between Crimea and Russia — the only access to the Sea of Azov. A flashpoint since 2014 and contested throughout the Russia–Ukraine war.
cp:kerch.recent: Traffic has collapsed to zero, down 98.3% against its own 90-day baseline, from a high of 50 vessels a day on May 18. The Black Sea has become a shooting gallery: strikes closed Odessa's ports, where war-risk premiums now price ships out of calling, a drone killed a crewman on a coal-hauling tanker, and Putin threatened to seize cargo ships.

mkt:tadawul.standing: The Arab world’s largest exchange by market value, dominated by Aramco. Trades Sunday to Thursday, so it opens the global week before Tokyo.
mkt:tadawul.recent: The index has drifted below its mid-June high through a summer of Gulf escalation: Houthi missiles hit Yemen's oil provinces and wounded 11 civilians in Najran, and a claimed strike on the Jazan refinery, which processes 400,000 barrels of crude daily, was followed by Saudi Arabia saying a fire at the Aramco facility in Jizan was extinguished. The Mecca defence pact signed with Turkey and Pakistan on 7 August left commitments undefined.

mkt:bist.standing: Türkiye’s only exchange. Priced in lira, so its index level carries the country’s inflation as much as its earnings — read the direction, not the number.
mkt:bist.recent: Ankara passed a law meant to end the PKK conflict on 10 August, and Turkey signed a joint defence pact with Saudi Arabia and Pakistan in Mecca on 7 August. Against that, drones struck the Turkish-operated Nadezhda near Novorossiysk and Turkey began rationing Bosphorus passage, raising war-risk costs on Black Sea trade.

mkt:dfm.standing: The Gulf’s main listing venue for property and banking. Moved from a Sunday–Thursday week to Monday–Friday in 2022, unlike Riyadh.
mkt:dfm.recent: The index sits below its Jun 18 high of 6270 after a month in which seven blasts in twenty minutes hit Jebel Ali port and Iran pressed new demands around the Strait of Hormuz, including an Iranian-controlled inbound lane — both threats to the transshipment traffic Dubai's listed logistics and banking names depend on. Gulf tourism is forecast to shed 137,000 jobs.

mkt:bursa-malaysia.standing: The world’s largest market for Islamic finance instruments, and the centre of the global sukuk trade.
mkt:bursa-malaysia.recent: The index has drifted lower since peaking at 1748 on Aug 5, the day before Gulf crude exports to Malaysia dipped on the Hormuz closure. Vessel transits through the strait have fallen to a fraction of normal, and the squeeze has since reached Malaysian refineries.

mkt:idx.standing: The exchange of the world’s largest Muslim-majority country, heavily weighted to commodities and banking.
mkt:idx.recent: The index sits near the bottom of a three-month slide, down about a fifth from its May high before a partial recovery from the June trough. The one Jakarta event with a clear market channel was Prabowo's nomination of a Bank Indonesia deputy as the new governor on 11 August, which lifted the rupiah slightly.

mkt:tse.standing: Asia’s largest exchange, and the first major market to price each trading day.
mkt:tse.recent: The index has climbed with the yen story. Toyota's quarterly profit hit $9.4 billion on a cheap yen and solid demand, and the Bank of Japan held rates at 1% on 31 July, keeping the currency weak enough to flatter exporter earnings. A joint US-Japan intervention on 3 August pushed the dollar to a one-month low, but the equity rally held.

mkt:hkex.standing: Where mainland Chinese companies meet foreign capital — the clearest daily read on sentiment toward China.
mkt:hkex.recent: The 64-day stretch has been dominated by China risk rather than Hong Kong's own economy: Beijing tightened drone exports into another trade clash with Washington, Trump set a polysilicon price floor targeting Chinese solar supply, and Typhoon Dolphin shut major ports and forced over a million evacuations before landfall. The index sits below where it started, near 25,460.

mkt:sse.standing: Mainland China’s main board. Largely closed to foreign investors, so it tracks domestic policy more than global risk appetite.
mkt:sse.recent: The index sits about 6.6% below its May 13 high of 4243, having bottomed at 3764 on July 17. Factory and services activity shrank in July on extreme weather and weak demand, and Typhoon Dolphin then forced port closures and the evacuation of over a million people before landfall. Beijing has also tightened drone exports, opening another trade clash with Washington.

mkt:krx.standing: Dominated by Samsung and SK Hynix — a proxy for the global semiconductor cycle.
mkt:krx.recent: Memory drives this index. Samsung reported profit up 1,814% on AI chip demand and warned of shortage through 2028; the Kospi's steepest three-day rout, bottoming Jul 30, was followed by its largest single-day gain ever, 18%. SK Hynix's $38B fab bet and 2027 capacity already sold out keep the swings wide.

mkt:bse.standing: Asia’s oldest exchange, founded 1875, and the benchmark for Indian equities.
mkt:bse.recent: The index sits near its Aug 6 high of 78,950 after a 4.3% climb over the window, easing 0.2% on the day. Two Mumbai stories sit under that: July inflation running hot on food, with onion prices up 22.54%, and reports that Tata Sons chairman Chandrasekaran may quit before an August 18 vote on the holding company's listing.

mkt:sgx.standing: Southeast Asia’s financial hub, weighted to banks and regional property.

mkt:twse.standing: TSMC alone is roughly a third of the index, which makes this the most concentrated major market on the map.
mkt:twse.recent: The index is up 11% over the quarter, with the low on 30 July falling within days of two Chinese coast guard ships drifting off Orchid Island, east of Taiwan, and the run to 45,940 has since resumed. Taipei says AI agents extracted passwords over four days in a hacking campaign, and Arizona has been pitching 100 Taiwanese investors on tax breaks to build beyond chips.

mkt:set.standing: Thailand’s benchmark, sensitive to tourism flows and regional energy prices.
mkt:set.recent: The index sits near the top of its 47-day range after climbing from May, with the day's fall coming amid a run of unsettled domestic news: the Nonthaburi school shooting that killed eight and prompted the Thai PM to promise stricter gun laws, Bangkok's reception of Min Aung Hlaing, and a crackdown on USDT transactions tied to scam compounds.

mkt:pse.standing: A small, domestically-driven market where remittance flows move the index.
mkt:pse.recent: The index sits below its 17 July high as the Sara Duterte impeachment trial reached Day 14, with a confidential fund list naming recipients such as Miggy Mango and Jay Kamote against disbursements recorded with zero results. A magnitude 6.3 earthquake struck the southern Philippines on 5 August.

mkt:asx.standing: Mining and banking. Often the first major market to react to Chinese demand data.
mkt:asx.recent: The index sits near its 6 August high after the RBA held rates steady on 11 August, with the housing market softening and a further hike still possible. The drag on the mining side is structural: China's steel stock is now old enough to recycle, shifting demand toward scrap and away from Australian iron ore.

mkt:jse.standing: Africa’s largest exchange by far, and the continent’s only one with a usable public daily series.
mkt:jse.recent: The index sits near the middle of its two-month range after peaking on Aug 7, with the sharpest drop coming on the final session. Nothing in the domestic record explains the fall; the one local pressure on view is electricity, where municipal bills rose up to 14% this month.

mkt:b3.standing: Latin America’s largest exchange, driven by iron ore, oil and Brazilian rates.
mkt:b3.recent: The index sits at its 66-day low of 167,500, down about 7% from its 12 May high, with the drop coinciding with a deteriorating relationship with Washington: on 4 August the US revoked the visa of Brazil's ambassador, saying it would restore it only if Brasília accepted its own envoy pick. Lula's nomination for a fourth term on 2 August added a domestic political question to the same window.

mkt:bmv.standing: Mexico’s benchmark, tightly coupled to US demand and the peso.
mkt:bmv.recent: The index sits about 6% below its mid-May level, having bottomed at 64,820 on Jun 10 and recovered only partly since. The input does not explain the decline: the Mexican news in this window runs to a screwworm outbreak that has passed 500 human cases, the $25 million US bounty on a cartel leader in Guadalajara, and restored diplomatic relations with Peru — none of them market events.

mkt:byma.standing: Priced in a currency that has lost most of its value repeatedly, so the index rises even in bad years. Direction over a day means something; the level does not.

mkt:tsx.standing: Energy, mining and banks — a commodity index wearing an equity index’s clothes.
mkt:tsx.recent: The index closed at a series high of 36,660 on Aug 12, up nearly 7% over the past 64 days from its May 19 low of 33,740. The coverage in this window — Canadian wildfires, a WestJet cabin-crew strike, AMD's purchase of Toronto's Taalas — does not explain the index's climb.

mkt:nyse.standing: The largest equity market on earth. Its close sets the tone every other market opens against.
mkt:nyse.recent: The index has climbed steadily to a high of 7758 on Aug 7 while the Gulf confrontation stayed short of war: Trump cancelled attacks on Iran's infrastructure on Aug 2, and talks with Iran to reopen the Strait of Hormuz were reported to be making progress. US missiles crippled a civilian cargo ship in the Gulf of Oman on Aug 11 without denting the level.

mkt:lse.standing: Most FTSE 100 revenue is earned abroad, so a falling pound tends to push the index up.

mkt:xetra.standing: Germany’s industrial and chemical base — Europe’s clearest export barometer.
mkt:xetra.recent: The index touched a series high of 26,390 on Aug 11 before easing 0.2%, up nearly 10% across the window. Commerzbank said on Aug 6 that teaming up with UniCredit could create value, softening Berlin's position that the takeover was a sovereignty threat, and Adidas reported strong growth on the World Cup.

mkt:euronext-paris.standing: Luxury goods and energy dominate — unusually exposed to Chinese consumer demand.
mkt:euronext-paris.recent: The index sits near its 8,726 high of Aug 10 after climbing roughly 9% over the window, and slipped 0.46% on the day. Nothing in the record explains the move: the French news of the period runs to jellyfish shutting 3.2 gigawatts of nuclear capacity at Gravelines, a record-hot June and July, and TotalEnergies buying Shell's European onshore renewables arm.

mkt:euronext-amsterdam.standing: The world’s oldest exchange, now carried largely by ASML.
mkt:euronext-amsterdam.recent: The index closed at a 67-day high on Aug 11, up about 10% since its May 12 low, and the day's move was slight. Nothing in the record explains the climb.

mkt:bme.standing: Spanish banks with heavy Latin American exposure make this a proxy for both regions.
mkt:bme.recent: The index reached 20,210 on Aug 11 and has climbed about 15% over the window, sitting near that high despite a run of political friction: Italy suspended Schengen against Spain on Jul 31 after roughly 72,000 people crossed into Ceuta, and Spain imposed reciprocal checks on Aug 7.

mkt:borsa-italiana.standing: Banks and utilities, and the market most sensitive to Italian sovereign debt spreads.
mkt:borsa-italiana.recent: The index climbed through a summer of Italian political friction without breaking stride, setting a high of 53,720 on 7 August — the day Spain imposed reciprocal border checks on Italy, a week after Rome suspended Schengen over the 72,000 people who rushed the Ceuta enclave. Milan dealmaking continued regardless: Bending Spoons agreed to buy Airtable for $1.28bn on 4 August.

mkt:six.standing: Nestlé, Roche and Novartis carry the index, which makes it defensive when the world turns risk-off.
mkt:six.recent: The index closed at 14450, down 0.86 percent on the day, after touching a 65-day high of 14630 on Aug 10. It is up roughly 10 percent over the window, having risen from a low of 13120 on May 12.

mkt:nasdaq-stockholm.standing: Nordic industrials and telecoms, and a useful early read on European capital spending.

mkt:tase.standing: Trades Sunday to Thursday. Heavily weighted to banks, defence and technology.
mkt:tase.recent: The index sits at 4,065, down 8.6% over the past 64 days, having fallen from a 4,463 high on May 25 to a 3,966 low on June 29 and recovered only partly since. Nothing in the available material explains the decline.

xag.standing: The price of an ounce of silver, tracked through a silver-backed token rather than a futures contract. Silver is both a monetary metal and an industrial one — it conducts better than any other element, and solar cells, electronics and brazing all compete for it.
xag.recent: The quote is $61.15 an ounce, about 6% above where the 31-day window opened. The window itself is unreliable: it records a low of 29.8 on Aug 6 and a high of 63.25 on Aug 8, a two-day doubling no physical silver market produced, which points to a feed gap rather than a move.

wiki-spain.standing: Wikipedia's article on Spain, and how many people read it each day. Attention to a country page rises when that country is the setting for something — a disaster, an election, a border crisis, or an event people travel to see.
wiki-spain.recent: Two Spanish stories ran through the window. Ceuta absorbed 72,000 crossings into a city of 84,000, with 57 bodies recovered, and Italy suspended Schengen over it before Spain imposed reciprocal checks on the Italian border. Then Wednesday's total eclipse crossed Burgos, Zaragoza and Teruel, where totality lasted 81 seconds.

poly-will-the-us-invade-iran-before-2027.standing: A Polymarket contract on whether the United States launches an invasion of Iran before 2027. The price is what traders will pay for that outcome, so it moves on the same news the region's oil, shipping and defence markets move on.
poly-will-the-us-invade-iran-before-2027.recent: The price has fallen from a 32% peak on Jul 19 to 18%, with its low of 16% on Aug 6 — the week Trump halted attacks on Iran's infrastructures and talks with Iran to reopen the Strait of Hormuz were reported to be making progress, with Iran, Oman and the US described as close to a deal.

poly-will-there-be-no-change-in-fed-inte.standing: What traders will pay for the outcome that the Federal Reserve leaves its policy rate unchanged. That rate sets the price of dollar credit, so mortgages, corporate borrowing and emerging-market debt all move behind it.
poly-will-there-be-no-change-in-fed-inte.recent: The Fed's July hold was read as hawkish, and on 7 August Trump again moved to fire Cook, reviving the fight over Fed independence. Conviction that rates stay put climbed from 39 on Aug 1 to 67 on Aug 13.

poly-us-iran-60-day-negotiation-period-e.standing: A Polymarket contract on whether Washington and Tehran hold to a fixed 60-day window for talks. The price is what traders will pay for that outcome, so it moves with each signal that the diplomatic track is holding or breaking.
poly-us-iran-60-day-negotiation-period-e.recent: The price has fallen from 75 on Aug 6 to 23 as the Hormuz track hardened: Trump said of the Strait, "We own it," and Iran kept reopening conditional, with 8 to 15 ships now crossing daily. On Aug 11 two Hellfire missiles crippled a civilian cargo ship in the Gulf of Oman.

poly-fed-rate-hike-in-2026.standing: A prediction market on whether the US Federal Reserve raises interest rates at any point in 2026. The price is what traders will pay for that outcome, so it moves with每 policy signal, inflation print and appointment fight that touches the Fed.

poly-will-alexandria-ocasio-cortez-win-t.standing: A Polymarket contract on whether Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez wins the 2028 US presidential election. Traders buy and sell shares that pay out if she does, so the price is what people will pay for that outcome, not a poll.

wiki-turkey.standing: Daily readership of the English Wikipedia article on Turkey, a rough gauge of how many people are looking the country up rather than of anything happening inside it. Attention spikes trace back to a story worth reading.
wiki-turkey.recent: The 22 July peak sits before this window's news, but the August traffic tracks two Turkish stories: on 7 August Saudi Arabia, Turkey and Pakistan signed the Mecca joint defence pact, whose obligations and nuclear guarantee are left undefined, and on 10 August Ankara passed a PKK disarmament law that never names Abdullah Öcalan's release.

stocks:AMZN.standing: Shares in the world's largest online retailer, which also runs Amazon Web Services, the biggest cloud computing provider. Its price tracks consumer spending, cloud demand and the enormous capital budgets behind both.
stocks:AMZN.recent: The stock ran from $226.70 on 29 July to a $284 high on 3 Aug before easing to $267.30, an 8% gain across the window. The coverage in this period concerns the company's build-out rather than its earnings: Amazon is funding a Fort Stockton gas plant whose 35 turbines could emit 33 million tons yearly to power datacentres, and Twitch opted every streamer into AI training by default.
